text:
Devon Levi came to Edmonton from Buffalo looking for a place to prove himself, and the record says he has found one: 10-2-0 in 12 starts, and a Gino Hard headline billing it as an Oilers record: 10 wins in 11 games. Under Mike Babcock, the Oilers have leaned on him through November.

The underlying numbers are good, not great. He has saved 3.5 goals more than his shots deserve (74th percentile), with a .902 save percentage. Most of that comes from easy and middling shots: .983 on low-danger looks against a league .963. The hard ones are the worry. He is at .674 on high-danger shots, a hair under the league's .687, and 14.2% of his saves turn into another shot within three seconds (league 10.8%). Rebounds like that are how a goalie gets beaten in bunches.

So the wins flatter him a little; a team scoring for him is part of that record. Still, a former 212th pick with a .952 college season at Northeastern is winning NHL games at a rate few expected. Watch the rebound rate: if it drops, the rest of his game holds up.
headline: Levi's fresh start in Edmonton
